gmail.name: Gmail
gmail.notes: Consumer Gmail attachment limit per message (Google Workspace may differ by admin policy).

outlook-web.name: Outlook on the web
outlook-web.notes: Default limit for Outlook.com / Outlook on the web (OWA) attachments unless a Microsoft 365 tenant policy raises or lowers it.

canvas-lms.name: Canvas LMS
canvas-lms.notes: Common default upload cap on Canvas course assignments (institution-configurable).

blackboard.name: Blackboard Learn
blackboard.notes: Typical assignment upload ceiling on many Blackboard Learn / Ultra courses; admins can set a different quota.

usps-online.name: USPS and similar gov portals
usps-online.notes: Many USPS, federal, and municipal online forms enforce a single-file PDF cap near 10 MB. Always check the form’s stated limit.

moodle.name: Moodle
moodle.notes: Moodle site and activity upload limits are set by the institution (often 2–50 MB). This page targets a conservative 10 MB assignment-style ceiling; raise quality only if your Moodle admin published a higher maxbytes.

whatsapp-document.name: WhatsApp document share
whatsapp-document.notes: WhatsApp allows large document sends (often up to ~100 MB depending on client), but mobile data and chat UX degrade above ~16 MB. This page targets a practical 16 MB delivery size for PDFs shared as documents — not media auto-compression.

slack.name: Slack
slack.notes: Paid Slack workspaces allow larger uploads, but free plans and mobile channel previews are harsh. Dense PDFs past ~1 MB routinely force “tap to download” and stall phone sidebars — this page targets that practical screen-sharing ceiling, not the marketing max.

teams.name: Microsoft Teams
teams.notes: Many Microsoft 365 tenants behave like a ~25 MB practical attachment budget for Teams chat and channel files (tenant policy can differ). Tuned for meeting-chat PDFs, not meeting recordings.

discord.name: Discord
discord.notes: Nitro-free Discord uploads are commonly capped near 10 MB (boost/Nitro raises it). Phone scans and slide decks blow past that quickly — Screen preset keeps homework and community PDFs shareable without Nitro.

telegram.name: Telegram
telegram.notes: Telegram can accept much larger bots/cloud files, but a practical ~20 MB document size keeps chat downloads reliable on mobile data when sharing PDFs as files (not compressed media).

google-drive.name: Google Drive
google-drive.notes: Drive storage quotas are separate; this page targets a practical ~100 MB comfort zone for browser upload fields and shared-link recipients on average connections. Milder Web quality (96 DPI) — not print masters.

dropbox.name: Dropbox
dropbox.notes: Dropbox plan caps vary widely; a practical ~50 MB PDF keeps web uploads and shared-link previews comfortable for collaborators without forcing desktop-sync-only workflows.

notion.name: Notion
notion.notes: Notion file embeds and uploads feel sluggish past a few megabytes in wiki pages. This page aims at a practical ~5 MB Screen target so attached PDFs open inside Notion without long spinners.

linkedin.name: LinkedIn
linkedin.notes: LinkedIn document posts and media uploads often allow large files near ~100 MB, but recruiters on phones abandon oversized decks. Mild Web quality keeps brand color while trimming export bloat.

zoom.name: Zoom
zoom.notes: Zoom in-meeting chat file shares are far tighter than cloud recording sizes. A practical ~20 MB PDF keeps handouts downloadable during the call on typical Wi-Fi.

wetransfer.name: WeTransfer
wetransfer.notes: Free WeTransfer transfers have a modest total-transfer comfort zone; targeting ~25 MB per PDF keeps single-file sends reliable without a paid plan when clients expect a simple download link.

github.name: GitHub
github.notes: GitHub warns and blocks oversized blobs around 25 MB for normal repository files (LFS is a separate path). Strip annotations from design-tool PDF dumps before committing specs.

icloud-mail.name: iCloud Mail
icloud-mail.notes: iCloud Mail attachment limits commonly land near ~20 MB (similar to Outlook consumer). Compress locally before attaching large scans or deck exports from Apple Mail / iCloud.com.

yahoo-mail.name: Yahoo Mail
yahoo-mail.notes: Yahoo Mail consumer attachments commonly fail near a ~25 MB total message budget (similar to Gmail). Scanned packets and deck exports trip Send even when page count looks small.

proton-mail.name: Proton Mail
proton-mail.notes: Proton Mail encrypts at rest on their side after you attach; this page still compresses locally first so sensitive PDFs never hit a third-party compress site. Practical ~25 MB attachment comfort for free/plus tiers unless your plan documents otherwise.

google-classroom.name: Google Classroom
google-classroom.notes: Classroom inherits Drive-like ceilings, but teachers and students on phones abandon oversized homework PDFs. Practical Screen target keeps submissions openable in the Classroom app without long spinners.

brightspace.name: Brightspace (D2L)
brightspace.notes: Many Brightspace / D2L courses enforce assignment upload caps near 10 MB (org-configurable). Phone worksheet photos routinely blow past that without a Screen pass.

schoology.name: Schoology
schoology.notes: K-12 Schoology assignments often inherit tight school-district upload ceilings near 5 MB. Grayscale Screen mode is intentional for worksheet photos.

gradescope.name: Gradescope
gradescope.notes: Gradescope accepts multi-page exam scans; a practical ~20 MB target keeps bubble sheets and handwritten pages uploadable without crushing OCR-critical contrast entirely.

jira.name: Jira
jira.notes: Atlassian Cloud Jira attachments are commonly limited near 10 MB per file (site admins can change it). Design PDFs and log dumps need a Screen/Web tradeoff before ticket upload.

confluence.name: Confluence
confluence.notes: Confluence page attachments and macros feel sluggish past ~10 MB in many Cloud sites. Mild Web quality keeps architecture PDFs embeddable without timing out the editor.

asana.name: Asana
asana.notes: Asana allows large task attachments on paid plans, but mobile task views stall on bloated PDFs. Practical Web comfort near 100 MB with annotation strip for design exports.

box.name: Box
box.notes: Box enterprise quotas vary; a practical ~50 MB PDF keeps browser uploads and shared-link previews comfortable for external reviewers without forcing desktop sync only.

onedrive.name: OneDrive
onedrive.notes: OneDrive/SharePoint can store huge files, but emailing a OneDrive link still fails when someone insists on a direct PDF attach under mail caps. Mild Web quality trims export bloat before share.

messenger.name: Facebook Messenger
messenger.notes: Messenger document sends on mobile are unreliable once PDFs climb past a practical ~25 MB comfort zone (client/version dependent). Screen/Web hybrid keeps receipts and forms shareable in chat.
